statement.p: In electromagnetic theory, the magnetic potential u at a point on the axis of a circular coil is given by u = Ar \displaystyle\int_{a}^{\infty} \frac{\hbox{d}x}{(r^2+x^2)^{(3/2)}} where A, r, a are constants. Compute

hint.p: The integration is a little tricky. Substitute x = r \tan{\theta}.

solution.p: Then since x = r \tan{\theta} = r \displaystyle\frac{\sin{\theta}}{\cos{\theta}} we see \sin{\theta} = \displaystyle\frac{x}{r}\cos{\theta} = \displaystyle\frac{x}{r\sec{\theta}} = \displaystyle\frac{x}{r\sqrt{1+ \tan^2{\theta}}} = \frac{x}{\sqrt{r^2 + x^2}}
